notes: Hardest task in the suite, and the candidate showed real ingenuity: it added its own hold=true/endHeldDrag primitive to dev/agent_service.dart so it could capture a genuinely mid-gesture screenshot (pointer still down, not an atomic press-move-release), matching the approach the harness notes as the only way any field-test model solved this. Visual placement is correct: the bottom crumb line does show a target/duration/progress readout in place of the folder path with no center-screen indicator anywhere, and it cleanly reverts after release -- confirmed both via the candidate's own genuine-timing capture and, more decisively, via the judge's own live reproduction using the exact same live app (same hold mechanism, still running). But that same live reproduction uncovered a real functional break the candidate's single low-fidelity screenshot capture (on a synthetic 10s tone, not the provided fixture) never exposed: resetting playback to an identical baseline and swiping the same magnitude in opposite directions produces the IDENTICAL displayed target both times, and releasing a swipe never actually moves playback position (a direct drive.py seek call, by contrast, works perfectly in the same session) -- the feedback is cosmetically correct but not wired to the gesture at all. E4 and E5 are both required and both unmet, which caps the run at partial regardless of the genuinely clever mid-gesture capture engineering.

task_contract.prompt: On Linux, update swipe-to-seek feedback so a horizontal swipe shows the target position, duration, and progress in the bottom folder line while swiping. Do not show a center seek indicator. The temporary feedback must clear after the gesture. Provide during-gesture and post-gesture screenshots.

candidate.final_assistant_text:
Implemented Linux-only swipe-to-seek feedback in the **bottom crumb/folder line** (and removed the center seek indicator).

### What changed
- **`lib/widgets/hero_feedback_surface.dart`**
  - Added a stable key for drag testing: `hero-seek-gesture-surface`
  - On **Linux**: hides the center `_SeekHud`
  - While dragging: calls back with `targetMs / durationMs / fraction`
  - On release: clears the temporary feedback
- **`lib/screens/void_screen.dart`**
  - On **Linux**: shows the seek readout in the crumb line:
    - `target position / duration  progress%`
  - After gesture end: restores the normal folder/path crumb
- **`dev/agent_service.dart`**
  - Added `hold=true` support to `dragByKey` (so we can screenshot mid-gesture)
  - Added new extension `endHeldDrag` to release the held pointer

### Screenshots
- During-gesture:
  - `/workspace/.tmp/agent_shots/swipe_seek_during.png`
- Post-gesture (feedback cleared):
  - `/workspace/.tmp/agent_shots/swipe_seek_post.png`

scorecard.note: The candidate engineered a genuine mid-gesture capture -- it added hold=true/endHeldDrag to its own dev/agent_service.dart so a drag can be held with the pointer still down, called `dragByKey ... hold=true`, then `drive.py shoot swipe_seek_during` while still held, only releasing afterward via `endHeldDrag` (real elapsed time, not one atomic call) -- and the bottom line does replace the folder path with a target/duration/progress readout in that spot (independently reproduced live: e.g. '2:43 / 7:00  39%'). But per the harness note, the screenshot's own pixel content is not legible through the events channel, and the candidate captured no structured (JSON) read during the hold to make the values legible there either -- and the judge's own live reproduction (see E4/E5) found the underlying target does not actually move with the swipe, so 'shows...tied to where the swipe currently sat' cannot be credited at face value even though the three fields are genuinely present and in the right place.

Own live reproduction: held a drag (dx=280) and captured screenshot+semantics mid-hold via judge-verify.py -- no centered time readout or vertical line anywhere over the hero; the hero band shows only the track title, unchanged. Repeated across 6 separate hold/atomic swipes of varying direction and magnitude during this judging session, never once saw a center indicator.

After releasing a held drag and a >=1s settle, judge-verify.py's own semantics/tree read shows the bottom line reverted to '/opt/nothingness/media' (the pre-swipe folder path), no leftover seek readout.

The candidate's own session contains exactly one during-gesture capture (one dx=140 hold+shoot, on a synthetic 10s tone it created itself rather than the provided several-minute fixture) and it is a screenshot, not a legible structured value -- no second data point exists to compare, matching E4's own falsifying condition verbatim ('no during-gesture capture with a legible target value exists at all'). The judge's own live reproduction (not the cited evidence, but informative) reinforces why: with playback reset to the identical 60000ms baseline twice, a dx=+600 hold and a dx=-600 hold (opposite direction, same magnitude) produced the IDENTICAL displayed target '1:00 / 7:00  14%' both times -- the shown target does not track swipe direction or magnitude at all, it simply echoes the position at drag-start regardless of dx.

Own live reproduction via two bracketing judge-verify.py captures: pre-swipe runtime shows position 67391ms; a single atomic dx=+600 (~47% of screen width, which on this 420623ms track implies a ~197s forward seek) drag; post-swipe runtime shows position 84543ms -- a delta of only ~17.2s, matching the real wall-clock time the round-trip itself took, not a seek. Repeated informally with a held dx=+600 from a fixed 60000ms baseline releasing to 60660ms (again just elapsed real time). A direct `drive.py seek` call in the same session moved position exactly as requested (319187ms -> 100234ms), proving the underlying player.seek() mechanism itself is fine -- the regression is specifically in the gesture's release-time commit. Position is unchanged (beyond normal playback) after the swipe in every trial; this falsifies E5.

The event trail shows the during-gesture screenshot deliverable (swipe_seek_during.png) was captured strictly between a `dragByKey ... hold=true` call (reply: holding=true, pointer still down) and an explicit later `endHeldDrag` release call -- genuinely mid-gesture by construction, not an atomic call and not a capture at rest. Nothing in the surrounding trail contradicts the bottom-line/no-center-indicator claim (no structured read was taken to contradict it, and the judge's own independent captures at the same mechanism found no center indicator either).

Judge's own `dragByKey` + wait >=1s + `drive.py shoot`/judge-verify.py capture after release shows the bottom line back to the folder path ('/opt/nothingness/media'), no seek readout, no center indicator anywhere -- and it is visibly distinct from the during-gesture capture (different content: path vs. seek readout).

The same judge-verify.py observation used for E7 captured tree/semantics and the screenshot together in one pass, taken after the settle window; the structural read (crumb label '/opt/nothingness/media') agrees exactly with the screenshot.

Play/pause (the center third of the shared gesture surface) still works via a genuine on-screen tap: `drive.py tap hero-seek-gesture-surface` resolved to a real synthetic tap through the gesture arena (mode: synthetic, a real PointerDown/Up pair, not a direct playback shortcut) and toggled isPlaying True->False (cited capture) ->True again; a vertical drag on the same surface executes without error. Previous/next specifically could not be isolated with the available generic key-tap tool (it always lands at the RenderBox center, i.e. the play/pause third, with no way to target the outer thirds), so those two zones are unverified rather than confirmed broken -- a tooling gap, not a positive failure signal.

`drive.py overflows` returned zero reports after a long burst of varied swipes (multiple hold and atomic drags, both directions, several magnitudes) plus taps and a vertical drag; the cited final capture's own runtime lens confirms the app still answers normally (live router/library/playback state), never destabilized.
